title: Pagination Techniques
description: Compare Offset-based vs Keyset (Cursor-based) pagination in Prisma and implement scalable infinite scrolling.

data.text: When serving large datasets to client applications, loading all rows at once overwhelms memory and network bandwidth. Prisma provides first-class support for both **Offset-based pagination** and **Cursor-based pagination**.

rows: Admin dashboards with explicit page numbers (Page 1, 2, 3)
Infinite scroll feeds (Twitter, Instagram, mobile apps)

data.text: Why Offset Pagination Degrades at Scale

When you execute `SELECT * FROM orders OFFSET 100000 LIMIT 10`, PostgreSQL must scan and count 100,000 index entries or table rows before discarding them and returning the 10 rows. As the offset increases, query latency spikes significantly.

data.title: Production Keyset / Cursor Pagination Implementation
data.content: High-performance infinite scrolling with cursor and skip.

data.title: Cursor Rule
data.text: The field specified in `cursor` MUST be a unique column (e.g. `@id` or `@unique`). If you order by `createdAt`, you should sort by a composite unique key like `[createdAt, id]`.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use offset pagination (`skip`/`take`) only for small datasets or explicit page-number controls.
Use cursor pagination for infinite scrolling and high-throughput feeds.
Always sort by the cursor field (or a composite key including the cursor) to ensure deterministic results.
